{"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=energy+cost+scaling+relations+memory+reliability+retention+time+thermodynamic+bounds&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"Molecular Simulation of Hydrogen Systems: From Properties and Methods to Applications and Future Directions.\", \"abstract\": \"This extensive review highlights the central role of classical molecular simulation in advancing hydrogen (H<sub>2</sub>) technologies. As the transition to a sustainable energy landscape is urgently needed, the optimization of H<sub>2</sub> processes, spanning production, purification, transportation, storage, safety, and utilization is essential. To this end, accurate prediction of thermodynamic, transport, structural, and interfacial properties is important for overcoming engineering challenges across the entire H<sub>2</sub> value chain. Experimental measurements, despite being the traditional way of obtaining these properties, can be limited by the distinctive nature of H<sub>2</sub>, harsh operating conditions, safety constraints, and extensive parameter spaces. Free from such limitations, classical molecular simulations, in the general frameworks of Monte Carlo and Molecular Dynamics, provide an optimal balance between computational efficiency and accuracy, bridging the gap between quantum mechanical calculations and macro-scale modeling. This review also systematically covers molecular simulation methods and force fields for computing key properties of H<sub>2</sub> systems, such as phase and adsorption equilibria and transport coefficients. Beyond property prediction, we explore how molecular simulation reveals fundamental mechanisms governing hydrate formation and dissociation, membrane permeations, and H<sub>2</sub> embrittlement. When possible, data from multiple sources are compared and critically assessed, while effort is put on evaluating the force fields used and methodological approaches followed in the literature. Finally, this review aims at identifying research gaps and future opportunities, emphasizing emerging approaches, such as molecular simulation in the era of artificial intelligence.\", \"doi\": \"10.1021/acs.chemrev.5c00617\", \"pmid\": \"41369684\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC12746421\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"…
